topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the framing for the lecture by welcoming students and setting out the learning objectives for cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional Modalities and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss standard cancer therapies including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic drugs, alongside their mechanisms of action, systemic toxicities, and drug-efflux resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Vulnerabilities and DNA Repair Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover therapeutic strategies that take advantage of specific vulnerabilities in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell-cycle checkpoint defects, and synthetic lethality in DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Kinase Inhibitors, Oncogene Addiction, and Targeted Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on targeting hyperactivated oncogenic kinases with small-molecule inhibitors and detail the mechanisms of acquired drug resistance, pathway bypass, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Antibody-Based Therapeutics and Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the design and clinical application of monoclonal antibodies that target cell-surface antigens directly or deliver targeted cytotoxic payloads as antibody-drug conjugates.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and Cell-Based Treatments
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis of tumor immunosurveillance and therapies that engage or re-engineer the host immune system, including checkpoint blockade, BiTEs, and CAR T-cells.

topics.label: Systemic Challenges, Historical Progress, and Future Directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the broader landscape of cancer treatment by examining clinical challenges, historical survival trends, emerging prevention strategies, and ethical considerations.
